description: Study 1: twelve questions where a known, externally documented consideration is often missing from a first answer. One predeclared source per case supports any candidate that names that consideration. Selector terms and sources were fixed before any run.

turns.question: I am 68 and want to take ibuprofen every day for knee arthritis. What should I know?
Is it fine to keep taking it daily for a few months?
What could I discuss with my doctor instead?

evidence_plan.reason: NHS guidance: long-term ibuprofen use in older adults carries kidney and stomach risks and needs medical review.

turns.question: How should I store user passwords in my web application's database?
Which hashing parameters should I choose?
How should the login endpoint handle repeated failed attempts?

evidence_plan.reason: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet: password storage must be combined with protection against automated and brute-force login attempts.

turns.question: My A/B test reached p = 0.04 after I checked the results every day. Can I ship variant B?
How should I plan the next experiment?
My manager wants daily updates on the next test. How do I handle that?

evidence_plan.reason: Evan Miller, How Not To Run an A/B Test: repeatedly checking significance inflates the false-positive rate unless the sample size is fixed or a sequential method is used.

turns.question: How can I use retrieval practice in my secondary school lessons?
How should I plan revision in the weeks before the exams?
How often should students revisit older topics?

evidence_plan.reason: Dunlosky et al. (2013), Psychological Science in the Public Interest: practice testing and distributed (spaced) practice both have high utility.

turns.question: Should I pay off my 3% mortgage early or invest the money in an index fund?
I recently lost part of my income. Does that change your advice?
How much should I keep in savings before doing either?

evidence_plan.reason: Bogleheads wiki, Paying down loans versus investing: an emergency fund and liquidity come before extra loan payments or investing.

turns.question: My fraud detection model reaches 98% accuracy on our dataset. Is it ready for production?
How should I split the data for the final evaluation?
The model performs worse on new transactions. Why might that be?

evidence_plan.reason: Kaufman et al. (2012), Leakage in Data Mining: information leaking from the target or the future inflates offline accuracy.

turns.question: Can I insulate the inside of my old solid brick wall with foil-backed insulation boards?
Which insulation material would you choose instead?
The wall already feels damp in winter. What should I check first?

evidence_plan.reason: Historic England, Insulating Solid Walls: impermeable internal insulation on solid walls can trap moisture and cause interstitial condensation.

turns.question: Can our school publish pupils' photos on the school website?
A parent now wants a photo removed. What do we do?
How should we record the permissions we have?

evidence_plan.reason: GDPR Article 7(3): consent can be withdrawn at any time and withdrawal must be as easy as giving it.

turns.question: Can I let a large pot of chili cool overnight on the stove before putting it in the fridge?
How do I cool it quickly next time?
Is it safe to reheat it if it was left out?

evidence_plan.reason: USDA FSIS, Leftovers and Food Safety: cooked food left in the danger zone for more than two hours should be discarded; large amounts must be divided to cool quickly.

turns.question: We back up our servers every night. Is that enough for disaster recovery?
What should our recovery runbook contain?
How do we know our recovery time objective is realistic?

evidence_plan.reason: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1: contingency plans, including restoration from backups, must be tested and exercised.

turns.question: I surveyed 200 volunteers about screen time and sleep. Can I conclude that screens cause poor sleep?
What study design would let me test the causal claim?
How should I describe my current finding in the report?

evidence_plan.reason: Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If: observational associations can reflect confounding or reverse causation.

turns.question: We plan to plant trees to offset our company's emissions. Is that a solid plan?
How should we report this in our sustainability report?
What should we look for in an offset provider?

evidence_plan.reason: Oxford Principles for Net Zero Aligned Carbon Offsetting: offsets need additionality and permanence, and emission reductions come first.
